name: What questions should I ask before hiring someone to move bathroom plumbing?

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask before hiring someone to move bathroom plumbing?
mainEntity.text: What questions should I ask before hiring someone to move bathroom plumbing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before hiring someone to move bathroom plumbing, ask very specific questions about scope, access, and restoration. Find out which fixtures can realistically move, whether the work will require slab cutting or opening walls, and how the contractor plans to handle drain slope and venting. Ask who is responsible for permits and inspections, and whether the estimate includes patching drywall, concrete, or subfloor after the rough-in. It is also smart to ask what happens if hidden damage is found once the bathroom is opened. A strong contractor should be able to explain the plumbing route, expected demolition, and the sequence of work from rough-in to finish. For Los Angeles remodels, also confirm the contractor understands local permit expectations and any building-specific restrictions if the home is a condo or townhouse. Clear answers up front reduce the chance of delays, change orders, and unfinished details later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask what fixtures can move, whether the work needs a permit, how slab or framing access will be handled, what the timeline is, and what finish repair is included. You should also confirm who handles inspection and whether the estimate covers hidden conditions.
